steps.body: Once the object is covered, the length is simply the number of units used. Count them carefully, one per placement.
steps.narration: Once the object is covered, the length is simply the number of units used. Count them carefully, one per placement.

widget.prompt: Cover this branch with one-unit blocks and count them as you go.
widget.successFeedback: Five blocks cover the branch — so the branch is five units long.
widget.alignFeedback: Line up zero with the object's starting end before measuring.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must touch end to end — no spaces and no covering the same part twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Every block must be the same size, or the count means nothing.

predict.prompt: Five same-size units exactly cover an object. How long is it?
predict.reveal: Length in units is the number of units it takes to cover the object — here, five. "One" counts the object itself, not its length; it is the units that get counted, and covering took five of them.

cml.actionGoal: Manipulate the model and track how it represents g1m count units.
invariants: The manipulated model and the measurement relationship for g1m count units must stay consistent.
misconceptions: Reading a length from appearance or position instead of from same-size units laid end to end.
cml.counterfactualPrompt: What change would make the model stop representing the same measurement?

widget.prompt: Exactly 6 same-size cubes cover a ribbon with no gaps and no overlaps. How long is the ribbon in cubes? Choose the key measurement idea.

options.feedback: That counts one unit more than were actually placed along the object.
Correct — the length is the number of same-size units that cover it end to end, which is 6.
That misses one of the units that helped cover the object.
That doubles the count, as if each unit were counted twice over.

steps.body: The count is a description of the object: it says how many of that unit fit along it.
steps.narration: The count is a description of the object: it says how many of that unit fit along it.

widget.prompt: Count a fresh path: cover it from 3 to 9 with six one-unit blocks.
widget.successFeedback: Six equal blocks cover the path, so its measurement is six units.
widget.alignFeedback: Line zero up with the path's starting edge before you begin counting.
widget.gapOverlapFeedback: The blocks must meet end to end; a gap misses length and an overlap counts it twice.
widget.unitFeedback: Choose one unit size and keep it for every block in this measurement.

widget.prompt: The path is 9 cubes long and the stick is 7 cubes long. How many cubes longer is the path? Use a fresh measurement clue.

commonErrors.feedback: That is the whole length of the path, not the extra it has beyond the stick.
That is the length of the stick, not the difference between the two.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Re-read the two lengths given, then compare them one step at a time.
